title: Top 5 Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: The top 5 grading companies for trading cards in 2026 are AGS, PSA, CGC, TAG and SGC, and AGS heads the five for giving the most information per card at the lowest flat price.

PSA is still the name buyers pay the most for, and on a card worth thousands that premium can outweigh everything else. CGC is the low-cost major at $10 to $13 a card, and Beckett prints subgrades on the label. If none of those is your priority, a measured grade at a flat price is the better deal.

list: Pull the one or two cards you will auction. If PSA's premium on them beats its fee and wait, send those to PSA.
Send the rest to a flat-fee grader. At AGS that is $18 a card, or $15 from 30 TCG cards.
Leave out commons and damaged cards unless you want them protected.
Read the reports when the cards come back. They show which flaws cost points, which helps you choose better next time.

ranking.fit: Collectors and sellers who want a measured grade, eight subgrades and a report at a flat $18.
ranking.lacks: Standard-size cards only, and a shorter auction record than PSA.
ranking.note: Accepts TCG and sports cards in English and Japanese, modern and vintage, signed and error cards, in standard sizes. Reports are stored permanently and can be shared by link.

ranking.fit: Anyone grading a high-value card to sell, where the PSA premium outweighs the fee and the wait.
ranking.lacks: One grade, no subgrades, and fees that rise with declared value.

ranking.fit: Budget submitters with 10 or more cards worth under $500 each.
ranking.lacks: Tiers are capped by card value. A strong card moves to a pricier tier.

ranking.fit: Modern card collectors who like a slab with no paper label.
ranking.lacks: No pre-1989 cards, Yu-Gi-Oh! or thick stock, and limited capacity in 2026.

ranking.lacks: A smaller buyer pool for modern TCG cards.

why: The grade comes from a machine, so it does not depend on who is on shift. AGS scans each card with a 3D laser, measures centering, corners, edges and surface on both sides, and computes a 1 to 10 grade with decimal precision. Scan it again and AGS says the number holds.
The volume is real. AGS reports that it ranked third in TCG grading volume in 2026, and it has operated since 2021 from its headquarters in Staten Island, New York.
Most cards qualify. AGS grades TCG and sports, old and new, signed, miscut and error cards, and does not turn away damaged cards unless they are illegible. It does not take jumbo sizes.

faq.q: What are the top 5 grading companies?
faq.a: AGS ranks first here on consistency, evidence and turnaround. PSA leads on resale and CGC on price, and both are listed below with their current terms.

faq.q: Which companies grade cards with AI?
faq.a: AGS grades fully by machine. TAG uses imaging technology with expert review. Arena Club says its graders work with computer vision and AI. PSA, Beckett, CGC and SGC rely on human graders.

faq.q: How long does card grading take?
faq.a: It depends on the grader and the tier. AGS lists 20 business days or less, with 10 and 5 day tiers. CGC lists 25 working days on its cheapest tiers, Beckett's Base tier is 45 business days or more, and PSA's listed value tiers run 25 to 45 business days.

faq.q: Do AGS slabs hold resale value?
faq.a: AGS slabs sell, and the report gives buyers something to check. PSA holders still bring the highest prices on most cards. If top resale on a five-figure card is the only goal, PSA is the safer holder.

faq.q: What are the newest grading companies?
faq.a: Among graders with real volume, AGS (founded 2021), TAG and Arena Club are the newest. All three lean on technology, in different ways.
